decisions.reason: As a low-risk complementary care item with modest aspiration levels and clear cross-selling value to the installed flooring base, it would likely be retained unless sales had plainly weakened.

The maintenance oil remains closely tied to the firm's core flooring system, so with industry growth and some organisational slack management would keep it while continuing to monitor whether the line meets expected repeat-demand levels.

Because this care line serves the narrower segment of oiled floors, its aspiration is more niche and its risk is somewhat higher, but it still fits the existing customer base well enough to justify retention for now.

The moisture-protection underlay supports installation quality and complements core floor sales, so boundedly rational management would usually keep it unless its results fell visibly below comparable accessory products.

This underlay foam is still the most vulnerable to withdrawal because it appears more substitutable and potentially overlapping with other underlays, but in the absence of clear failure it is still more likely to be kept than dropped.
